citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The facility was unable to produce a written Program of Veterinary Care at the time of inspection; the facility director
stated that there may have been one at one time before she took over, but she did not have it or couldn't locate it.
A written program of veterinary care is required to ensure that there is an expectation about the care provided to all
animals. Failure to establish and maintain a written program of veterinary care can decrease the ability to ensure optimal
care of the animals. A written program of care must be established and maintained so that the licensee has a plan for
providing adequate preventative care and treatments when needed, including emergency, weekend and holiday care.
TO BE CORRECTED BY 07/30/2026

The licensee does not have complete acquisition records for birds at the facility; although names of the persons/entities
from whom birds are obtained is present, other missing information varies (addresses, license information/driver's license
and state) and none of the records presented contain all of the required information.
Complete documentation of acquisition and disposition is required for all animals to ensure their humane use. The
licensee must make, keep and maintain records or forms which fully and correctly disclose the information as detailed in
Part 2, Subpart G, Section 2.75(b)(1)(i-vii) of the Animal Welfare Act and Animal Welfare Regulations for animals
purchased or otherwise acquired, owned, held, leased or otherwise in his or her possession or under his or her control, or
which are transported, sold, euthanized or otherwise disposed of by that licensee. The records shall include any offspring
born of any animal while in his or her possession or under his or her control.
TO BE CORRECTED BY 07/30/2026 AND GOING FORWARD

citations.desc: Environment enhancement to promote psychological well-being.
citations.narrative:
Although the licensee is currently providing appropriate enrichment for the birds on site, the Avian Environment
Enhancement Plan does not include special considerations for birds requiring special attention. The verbiage from Part 3,
Subpart G, Section 3.154(c) is pasted into the plan, but the plan does not actually describe the enrichment measures
planned for the categories of birds with special considerations.
Complete enrichment plans are required to promote psychological well-being of the avian species at the facility. The
licensee must further develop, document and follow a more complete, species appropriate plan for environmental
enhancement adequate to promote the psychological well-being of birds, including special considerations. The plan must
be approved by the attending veterinarian and, at a minimum, must address social grouping, environmental enrichment,
special considerations, restraint, and exemptions to the plan.
TO BE CORRECTED BY 07/30/2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility director.
